summary: Validated decision-gated record for EnableVirtualization under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System. The clean Win25H2Clean baseline confirmed the live value, the repo security notes document the value and meanings, the path-aware static pass found exact current-build ntoskrnl.exe value hits plus adjacent EnableLUA and EnableInstallerDetection hits, and the tools-hardened path-aware ETW lane completed shell-safe but stayed a clean no-hit. The same path-aware runtime lane on the secondary profile reproduced the no-hit result, and a Linux KVM Procmon replay with a dedicated UAC/policy burst also produced a real CSV with zero matching lines. A KVM local-KD disassembly and string-dump follow-up on the running guest then showed the same current-build `PsBootPhaseComplete` cluster opening `\Registry\Machine\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System` and staging `EnableLUA`, `EnableVirtualization`, and `EnableInstallerDetection` directly. A later recovery-backed KVM Procmon replay reopened the elevated guest shell automatically and still returned zero intended-path or family hits. A follow-up KVM Procmon bootlog probe then completed a real reboot cycle, but Procmon returned exit code 1 for both `/EnableBootLogging` variants, left Procmon state unchanged, and skipped bootlog conversion with no PML or CSV. A later QGA-launched WPR boot registry trace then retained five exact quoted `EnableVirtualization` QueryValue hit lines and normalized them against the intended `Policies\System` target path, closing the runtime-read gap while keeping the record research-only and non-actionable.

setting.name: Enable Virtualization
setting.casual_explanation: Enable Virtualization controls legacy UAC file and registry virtualization under the Policies\System branch.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track it when studying legacy app compatibility, UAC virtualization, and adjacent policy-system behavior.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The lane now has exact docs, phase-0 existence, exact current-build static hits, shell-safe runtime follow-ups across ETW and repeated KVM Procmon transports, a failed-but-informative KVM Procmon bootlog attempt, a live KVM local-KD inspection that confirms the current-build policy-family path directly, and a QGA-launched WPR boot trace that retains five exact quoted `EnableVirtualization` QueryValue hit lines. The retained WPR hit lines do not print the full registry path, so the normalized bundle binds them to the intended `Policies\System` target path supplied to the run; that path was already independently corroborated by the earlier static and local-KD work. The record therefore no longer lacks runtime attribution, but it still remains a research-only legacy UAC virtualization control rather than a supported end-user surface.
setting.professional_notes: Phase-0 existence confirmed EnableVirtualization on the live Win25H2Clean baseline with preview value 1. The repo security notes document the value and meanings in Docs/security/security.md. The path-aware static pass over the narrowed binary set found an exact EnableVirtualization hit in ntoskrnl.exe, plus exact adjacent EnableLUA and EnableInstallerDetection hits in the same binary, while the VBS collision remained isolated to winload.exe through EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity. The current-build Ghidra export kept EnableVirtualization, EnableLUA, and EnableInstallerDetection in the same naturally resolved ntoskrnl.exe function. A tools-hardened path-aware ETW lane then ran short and split policy/UAC bursts on RegProbe-Baseline-ToolsHardened-20260330 and produced real ETL/CSV outputs, but it still returned a clean no-hit for both the exact value name and the intended path. A secondary-profile replay on Win25H2Clean-B reproduced the same shell-safe no-hit. A Linux KVM Procmon replay then ran a dedicated UAC/policy burst, produced a real 300881-line CSV, and still returned zero path or value matches for EnableVirtualization. A debugger-assisted KVM local-KD follow-up then attached to the live guest kernel, disassembled `PsBootPhaseComplete`, and showed a current-build `ZwOpenKey` / `ZwQueryValueKey` cluster loading the live key-path literal `\Registry\Machine\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System` together with adjacent live value-name literals `EnableLUA`, `EnableVirtualization`, `EnableInstallerDetection`, `TypeOfAdminApprovalMode`, `UACInstalled`, and `DevOverrideEnable`. A later recovery-backed KVM Procmon replay explicitly started from a closed elevated guest shell, reopened that shell through the hardened host runner, produced a fresh 228130-line CSV, and still returned zero lines containing `Policies\System`, `EnableVirtualization`, `EnableLUA`, or `EnableInstallerDetection`. A follow-up KVM Procmon bootlog probe then completed a real reboot cycle, but the current guest returned exit code 1 for both direct and minimized `/EnableBootLogging`, left Procmon state pointed at the prior runtime logfile, and skipped bootlog conversion with no PML or CSV to review. The 2026-04-13 QGA WPR boot-registry follow-up first exposed an over-broad substring match problem because `EnableVirtualizationForInprocServer` and `EnableVirtualizationForInprocHandler` were being retained alongside the target value. The guest normalizer was then tightened to require an exact quoted value-name match. The corrected rerun retained exactly five quoted `EnableVirtualization` QueryValue hit lines, rebooted cleanly, and produced a normalized bundle with five `QueryValue` events under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System`. That target path is bound from the explicit run input rather than printed verbatim in the retained raw tracerpt hit lines, but the earlier static and local-KD evidence had already fixed the current-build read site to the same `Policies\System` path. Within this repo, that closes the runtime_no_read gap without turning the record into a shipped tweak.

The record therefore no longer lacks runtime attribution. It remains intentionally held because this is a research-only legacy UAC virtualization control that is not mapped to a supported app surface.
